newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids little changed, helped by weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids little changed, helped by weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were little changed again Thursday in moderate trade, with hot weather scorching the East Coast boosting prospects for better utility demand, industry sources said.

"Utilities are going to have to be looking to replace some of the barrels they're burning this week," said one cash trader, noting several utilities on the East Coast and Florida already were testing the market for price.
A Florida utility awarded its tender for up to 350,000 barrels of 2.5 percent for August 1 delivery at $15.45. Traders said the utility may soon tender for some one percent.
U.S. Gulf one percent was unchanged to down slightly at $15.75 a barrel, while three percent notionally held steady at $13.25-50.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was flat to slightly higher at $16.25, with good generation demand and still-high city gate gas prices helping low sulphur sentiment, traders said.
NYH July one percent paper slipped about a quarter to $16.20-30 on weaker crude, while August paper was talked down slightly at $16.10-20 and Q4 modestly weaker at $16.50-60.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was unchanged in the high-$17 area though some thought the grade was valued in the low-$18s.
High sulphurs in New York were stable, with 2.2 percent still quoted at $14.50-75.

New York city gate swing gas prices tumbled about a dime Thursday to the low-$2.50s/mmBtu, or $15.94 a barrel equivalent, on forecasts for more seasonal weekend weather. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was down a similar amount to $2.22/mmBtu, or $13.99 a barrel.
